note: The CLOSED check vocabulary for git-native build receipts (work-item 081KYYJEJ4X08QG0R003P8GXSY).
A receipt may NAME a check from this file; it may never DEFINE one. An open vocabulary
would let a signer attest `everything-is-fine=pass` — true, signed, and constraining
nothing, which is the vacuity class this repo treats as a defect rather than a stub.
`verify-build-receipt.ts` refuses `unknown-check` for any id absent here.
ADDING A ROW is a real decision: it means a signer may henceforth make a signed claim
about that id, and every peer will accept the id as meaningful. Each row must name the
EXACT command a `pass` claims to have run to completion with a zero exit status.
The command is documentation for the human running it, not something any tool executes —
nothing in the verifier runs these, and nothing may, because a verifier that ran the
build would be a gate wearing a receipt's clothes.
